drhp.business: Valor Estate is a Mumbai Metropolitan Region-focused real estate developer specializing in large-scale urban regeneration, with core competencies in land aggregation, securing clear land titles, and property development undertaken in partnership with established developers. The company has developed a mix of office, luxury housing, social housing, retail and hospitality assets, and following the demerger of its hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited, it now concentrates on core real estate development including residential, commercial and redevelopment projects in MMR and a new project in Goa.
drhp.end_markets: Mumbai Metropolitan Region|Delhi Aerocity micro-market (pending acquisition)|Goa (Dona Paula, DBFOT project)
drhp.expansion: The Prestige Place, Worli (~18-acre urban regeneration, JV with Prestige) had its site clearance process fully completed during the year. Commercial portfolio expansion comprises option agreements for BKC 101 (~0.8 million sq. ft., completion 2028) and Prestige Mahalakshmi (~1.10 million sq. ft., completion 2029), both executed by the Prestige Group. At Bandra (W), construction of transit camps was completed, unlocking over two million sq. ft. of commercial area for development. At Lonavala, a 400-acre golf-course township with the Prestige Group is expected to commence development in the next financial year, with land largely acquired. The Government of Goa awarded the Company a Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer project for an International Convention Centre, Convention Hotel and associated facilities at Dona Paula, with the Concession Agreement executed. Subsequent to year-end, shareholders approved the proposed acquisition of Bamboo Hotel and Global Centre (Delhi) Private Limited, the project company for a mixed-use hospitality and commercial development at Aerocity, New Delhi.

litigation.note: A long-standing title dispute over the Mira Road land was litigated before the Bombay High Court and was resolved in the Company's favour during the year, per the Chairman/MD message.

drhp.mdna: Fewer homes were sold nationally but aggregate value of homes sold rose, reflecting a supply deficit concentrated in the affordable segment and continuing premiumisation.|Demand in affordable and mid-income segments is latent rather than absent; recent easing of interest rates should catalyse a gradual recovery in these categories, with CY26 positioned as a constructive year across all product segments.|The Company's participation in the BMC Project Affected Persons scheme is positioned to address the structural affordable-supply gap directly.|MMR is the largest housing market in India (30.1% of new launches across top seven cities in CY25); muted launches following CY24 decline have kept inventory overhang within a healthy seventeen-month range.|MMR per-capita income and infrastructure investment (Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link, Coastal Road, Navi Mumbai International Airport, Metro expansion) are converting peripheral land into more central, valuable land, benefiting developers holding land in the path of connectivity, including the Company's Mira Road holdings.|Demand continues to skew toward the premium segment in MMR, consistent with land cost being the highest proportion of project cost in the country.|Prime office rents in Bandra Kurla Complex recorded the strongest growth among global markets tracked by CBRE (22% year on year), supporting the Company's commercial interests at BKC 101 and Mahalaxmi.|Aerocity, New Delhi is a supply-constrained, high-value commercial and hospitality precinct with administratively scarce land, sustained rental premia, and occupancy above 95% in the post-pandemic period, relevant to the Company's proposed acquisition there.|Indian hospitality sector average daily rates and occupancy are at record highs, with new supply lagging demand in upscale/luxury segments.|Development pipeline described by management as 'one of the deepest' in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.|The Prestige Place, Worli — one of the largest urban regeneration projects in South Mumbai, with site clearance completed during the year and balance structures expected to be vacated in H1 of the next FY.|Commercial portfolio option agreements: BKC 101 (~0.8 million sq. ft., completion 2028) and Prestige Mahalakshmi (~1.10 million sq. ft., completion 2029), both offering annuity revenue potential.|Lonavala 400-acre golf-course township with the Prestige Group expected to commence development in the next financial year.|BMC Project Affected Persons scheme at approximately 13,374 housing units, among the largest developments in Mumbai, with agreements executed and conveyance to BMC completed.|Proposed acquisition of Bamboo Hotel and Global Centre (Delhi) Private Limited, the project company for a mixed-use hospitality and commercial development at Aerocity, New Delhi.

risks.note: Core business model depends on aggregating brownfield land in a mature city, where complex title histories, multiple stakeholders and extended approval chains can defer revenue and extend the period capital is committed without return.

risks.note: A substantial part of the portfolio is executed through JVs, joint development arrangements and option structures; pace of construction, launch timing, delivery quality, and (for options) when the Company's economic interest crystallises depend on counterparties the Company does not unilaterally control, and a partner's financial difficulty or execution failure would affect outcomes directly.
risks.risk: Partner and counterparty risk in joint ventures and option structures

risks.note: The Company and certain group entities are party to legacy claims and third-party disputes from historical transactions with inherent timing and outcome uncertainty, within a continually evolving regulatory framework covering real estate regulation, development control, environmental clearance, taxation and listed-company obligations.
risks.risk: Legal and regulatory risk from legacy claims and evolving regulation

risks.note: The Dona Paula concession is the Company's first material commitment outside MMR and first under a DBFOT structure, introducing unfamiliar regulation, a governmental counterparty, coastal/environmental clearance requirements and an operating component; the proposed Aerocity acquisition would extend the Company into an operating leasehold asset dependent on air-traffic-correlated demand and remains subject to lender consent outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: Execution risk on new formats and geographies (Goa DBFOT concession and proposed Aerocity acquisition)

risks.note: Rising sea levels, greater temperature volatility and more frequent extreme weather events pose structural risks to asset durability, construction supply chains and urban habitability; the portfolio is concentrated in a coastal metropolitan region and the newest commitment is on a coastal site in Goa.
risks.risk: Climate and environmental risk on coastal assets

risks.note: Institutional knowledge of specific land parcels, approval pathways and stakeholder relationships is concentrated in a relatively small number of individuals; the hospitality demerger also transferred associated manpower to Advent Hotels International Limited.

Revenue on a substantial part of the portfolio is recognised on completion or on satisfaction of defined milestones, so reported revenue and profitability can vary materially between periods for reasons of project timing rather than underlying business performance, making period-on-period comparison a poor guide to trajectory.

- Goa (Dona Paula, DBFOT project)

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Fewer homes were sold nationally but aggregate value of homes sold rose, reflecting a supply deficit concentrated in the affordable segment and continuing premiumisation.
- Demand in affordable and mid-income segments is latent rather than absent; recent easing of interest rates should catalyse a gradual recovery in these categories, with CY26 positioned as a constructive year across all product segments.
- The Company's participation in the BMC Project Affected Persons scheme is positioned to address the structural affordable-supply gap directly.
- MMR is the largest housing market in India (30.1% of new launches across top seven cities in CY25); muted launches following CY24 decline have kept inventory overhang within a healthy seventeen-month range.
- MMR per-capita income and infrastructure investment (Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link, Coastal Road, Navi Mumbai International Airport, Metro expansion) are converting peripheral land into more central, valuable land, benefiting developers holding land in the path of connectivity, including the Company's Mira Road holdings.
- Demand continues to skew toward the premium segment in MMR, consistent with land cost being the highest proportion of project cost in the country.
- Prime office rents in Bandra Kurla Complex recorded the strongest growth among global markets tracked by CBRE (22% year on year), supporting the Company's commercial interests at BKC 101 and Mahalaxmi.
- Aerocity, New Delhi is a supply-constrained, high-value commercial and hospitality precinct with administratively scarce land, sustained rental premia, and occupancy above 95% in the post-pandemic period, relevant to the Company's proposed acquisition there.
- Indian hospitality sector average daily rates and occupancy are at record highs, with new supply lagging demand in upscale/luxury segments.
- Development pipeline described by management as 'one of the deepest' in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
- The Prestige Place, Worli — one of the largest urban regeneration projects in South Mumbai, with site clearance completed during the year and balance structures expected to be vacated in H1 of the next FY.
- Commercial portfolio option agreements: BKC 101 (~0.8 million sq. ft., completion 2028) and Prestige Mahalakshmi (~1.10 million sq. ft., completion 2029), both offering annuity revenue potential.
- Lonavala 400-acre golf-course township with the Prestige Group expected to commence development in the next financial year.
- BMC Project Affected Persons scheme at approximately 13,374 housing units, among the largest developments in Mumbai, with agreements executed and conveyance to BMC completed.
- Proposed acquisition of Bamboo Hotel and Global Centre (Delhi) Private Limited, the project company for a mixed-use hospitality and commercial development at Aerocity, New Delhi.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Prestige Place, Worli (~18-acre urban regeneration, JV with Prestige) had its site clearance process fully completed during the year. Commercial portfolio expansion comprises option agreements for BKC 101 (~0.8 million sq. ft., completion 2028) and Prestige Mahalakshmi (~1.10 million sq. ft., completion 2029), both executed by the Prestige Group. At Bandra (W), construction of transit camps was completed, unlocking over two million sq. ft. of commercial area for development. At Lonavala, a 400-acre golf-course township with the Prestige Group is expected to commence development in the next financial year, with land largely acquired. The Government of Goa awarded the Company a Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer project for an International Convention Centre, Convention Hotel and associated facilities at Dona Paula, with the Concession Agreement executed. Subsequent to year-end, shareholders approved the proposed acquisition of Bamboo Hotel and Global Centre (Delhi) Private Limited, the project company for a mixed-use hospitality and commercial development at Aerocity, New Delhi.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- resource (land bank): Undeveloped land bank in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region spans more than 570 acres, assembled at historical cost in a market where land cost as a proportion of project cost is the highest in the country — evidence: '570 acres of land' / land cost is highest-in-country proportion of project cost.
- licence/regulatory: Mira Road land title dispute was conclusively resolved in the Company's favour by the Bombay High Court, giving complete legal certainty over a strategic asset — evidence: 'the long-standing title dispute relating to the Mira Road land was conclusively resolved in our favour by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court.'
- distribution: Mira Road land sits directly on the alignment of the Mumbai Coastal Road North Project and is presently serving as a casting yard, with rental income now commencing from that use — evidence: 'the Company's Mira Road land is presently serving as a casting yard' and 'rental income commencing from the casting yard serving major infrastructure works.'
- customer lock-in: Business partnerships with Prestige Estates Projects Ltd., Godrej Properties Ltd., Larsen & Toubro Ltd. and Lodha Ltd. give access to joint development execution capacity the Company does not itself need to build — evidence: named partnerships listed in Corporate Overview; Godrej Avenue Eleven Tower B launch and Tower A top slab cast with Godrej Properties JV; Ten BKC joint development with Adani Realty received full Occupancy Certificate.
- licence/regulatory [planned]: Government of Goa awarded the Company the International Convention Centre, Convention Hotel and associated facilities at Dona Paula on a Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer basis, with the Concession Agreement executed — evidence: 'the Concession Agreement has since been executed' — against it: project not yet built.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Development portfolio, land bank and revenue are overwhelmingly concentrated in MMR; any localised macroeconomic deceleration, adverse regulatory or policy shift, or prolonged demand slowdown there would disproportionately affect revenue and financial performance.
- Core business model depends on aggregating brownfield land in a mature city, where complex title histories, multiple stakeholders and extended approval chains can defer revenue and extend the period capital is committed without return.
- A substantial part of the portfolio is executed through JVs, joint development arrangements and option structures; pace of construction, launch timing, delivery quality, and (for options) when the Company's economic interest crystallises depend on counterparties the Company does not unilaterally control, and a partner's financial difficulty or execution failure would affect outcomes directly.
- The Company and certain group entities are party to legacy claims and third-party disputes from historical transactions with inherent timing and outcome uncertainty, within a continually evolving regulatory framework covering real estate regulation, development control, environmental clearance, taxation and listed-company obligations.
- The Dona Paula concession is the Company's first material commitment outside MMR and first under a DBFOT structure, introducing unfamiliar regulation, a governmental counterparty, coastal/environmental clearance requirements and an operating component; the proposed Aerocity acquisition would extend the Company into an operating leasehold asset dependent on air-traffic-correlated demand and remains subject to lender consent outside the Company's control.
- Rising sea levels, greater temperature volatility and more frequent extreme weather events pose structural risks to asset durability, construction supply chains and urban habitability; the portfolio is concentrated in a coastal metropolitan region and the newest commitment is on a coastal site in Goa.
- Institutional knowledge of specific land parcels, approval pathways and stakeholder relationships is concentrated in a relatively small number of individuals; the hospitality demerger also transferred associated manpower to Advent Hotels International Limited.
- Revenue on a substantial part of the portfolio is recognised on completion or on satisfaction of defined milestones, so reported revenue and profitability can vary materially between periods for reasons of project timing rather than underlying business performance, making period-on-period comparison a poor guide to trajectory.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Accelerate execution across ongoing developments.
- Advance construction at The Prestige Place, Worli.
- Progress the Project Affected Persons (PAP) project with BMC.
- Expand the commercial portfolio (BKC 101, Prestige Mahalakshmi).
- Unlock value at Mira Road and across the wider land bank.
- Pursue selective partnerships that enhance returns while maintaining capital efficiency.
- Focus capital allocation and steady monetisation of an extensive land bank.
- Concentrate on core real estate development following the hospitality demerger into Advent Hotels International Limited.
